statement.p: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve \displaystyle y^2 = \frac{x^{2}}{xy + 2} at (2,1)

p.em: (Enter undef if the slope is not defined at this point.)

static.solution: \frac{dy}{dx}\big|_{(2,1)}. Implicit differentiation yields: 2y\frac{dy}{dx}= \frac{2 x (xy + 2) - x^{2}(x\frac{dy}{dx}+y)}{(xy + 2)^2}. Given the complexity of the above equation, we first want to substitute 2 for x and 1 for y (the coordinates of the point where we are constructing our tangent line), then solve for \frac{dy}{dx}. Substitution yields: 2(1) \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2 (2) ((2)(1) + 2) - 2^{2}(2\frac{dy}{dx} + 1)}{((2)(1) + 2)^2}, or, 2 \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{16 - 4 (2 \frac{dy}{dx} + 1)}{16}. Solving for \frac{dy}{dx}, we have: \frac{dy}{dx} = 0.3 .
